propositions: Event-derivation readers must compute agent-process metrics (attempts-per-ticket, first-pass verification rate, rework at 7/30 days, reopen-recovery, revert-linked recovery) over the durable ticket event store including compaction-retired events, while escalation and cross-agent handoff metrics remain out-of-scope and report Unavailable.

Metrics requiring per-event or multi-occurrence data (attempts, rework windows, reopen counts) must read raw event files using existing reducer helpers (event_sort_key, is_active_event, RETIRED_SUFFIX) rather than compiled state, because compiled state preserves only terminal values.

Metrics for which a single terminal value suffices (first-pass rate via absence of last_reopened_at, revert-recovery via reverts[] list) must read compiled state from reduce_ticket to avoid reinventing file-listing logic.

Unit tests must verify that a fixture ticket claimed by two distinct sessions yields attempts_per_ticket==2, a closed→open→closed transition 3 days apart counts in rework_within_days(7) but not at 10 days, and a revert targeting STATUS or COMMITS is counted by revert_recovery while a revert targeting COMMENT is not.
Empty-range queries must return None (reported as Unavailable), and populated ranges with zero qualifying events must return 0 (measured zero), distinguished via the metric registration.
All metrics register into the registry with source=structural and confidence=high, authoritative, using HLC filename timestamps for exact date-range bucketing.
